notes:
BLOCKED (HELPER_MISSING): the pinned upstream exposes a simulated mobile-base command publication but no acknowledged ROS stop, so a RosDriver cannot establish the safe state that R2 requires. Last gate run 2026-11-05T08:45:08Z, backend fake, report digest sha256:01d49b2e9adf95dfcd7af0b69b6f18cc8a8d1c079f4fa93352ad9da7fd9099e3: G1 pass Layout and isolation; G2 pass Lock; G3 pass Strict resolve; G4 pass Provenance; G5 pass Reference; G6 fail Behaviour with G6.ESTOP_FAILED: mhs.safety.estop status failed, MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, estop 'engaged' expected engaged or software_only, the latch stays engaged; G7 pass Native surface; G8 fail Protocol and surface with G8.CONFORMANCE (MHS-Sim CL2, failing required test SAFE-028) and G8.TEST (SAFE-028 e-stop receipt failed, safe_state_achieved=false in the receipt, mhs.safety.status and the driver safety_status); G9 skip G9.NOT_RUN. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings and no G1 warnings.

WHAT WAS AUTHORED: a configuration-only ROS 1 RosDriver with no Python native and no native.py, because the upstream is a C++ catkin node. The primary wire surface is the flat 60-element Float64MultiArray on /dog/gazebo_pve_controller/command: SimulatedHardware::PublishCommand writes five twelve-element blocks (desired positions, kp, desired velocities, kd, feed-forward torque) at dog_ros/src/hardware/SimulatedHardware.cpp:59-75, and GazeboPVEController::commandCB rejects any other length and copies those blocks at gazebo_pve_controller/src/gazebo_pve_controller.cpp:288-310. The launch remaps the private endpoints to /dog/imu, /dog/joint_states and /dog/gazebo_pve_controller/command at dog_ros/launch/control.launch:10-12. Observations: JointState positions on /dog/joint_states (sensor_msgs/JointState; the callback requires twelve entries and derives velocity from position at SimulatedHardware.cpp:94-120), IMU orientation/angular velocity/linear acceleration on /dog/imu (sensor_msgs/Imu; dog_model/urdf/dog.gazebo:59-62) and ground-truth torso position on /ground_truth/state (nav_msgs/Odometry; dog.gazebo:41-45 and dog_world.launch:52-53). The default controller order and the twelve joint names are dog_model/config/controllers.yaml:7-19; the optional fourteen-joint tail configuration is NOT COVERED.

WHY THE HELPER CANNOT COMPLETE THIS SURFACE: a search of the pinned clone finds no advertiseService, actionlib server or SimpleAction; the only ROS service reference is the spawn_model comment, and no stop, pause, reset or hold service exists. The package therefore leaves safety_bindings empty and declares no safe-state action instead of fabricating one. A zero-valued 60-element frame is not a safe state: it removes the PD hold and the controller clamps only the resulting torque to the URDF effort limit (gazebo_pve_controller/src/gazebo_pve_controller.cpp:247-254); a zero frame can let the quadruped fall. A rosbridge publication is transmission evidence only (the action output is published=true, confirmed=false). The shipped dog_ros_node entry point calls only test_DynamicsDiff and constructs no SimulatedHardware (dog_ros/src/main.cpp:1-8), and the one executable is built from all src/*.cpp including the tests (dog_ros/CMakeLists.txt:27-29,158), so no shipped process runs the publisher or control loop. A live run would need a controller process outside this package, and even then the missing acknowledged stop means the e-stop receipt is failed with the latch engaged; the operator must reconcile the simulation externally and reset with mhs.safety.reset.

RISK AND SAFETY: risk is R2 because the frame drives a mobile quadruped; the card floor is R0 but the mobile-base class is R2. The device is simulated, so no estop_physical_ref is claimed and none exists in the clone. This is a genuine upstream stop gap, not a fake feature. The package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run ros-wave-c-115); driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null, no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, no Gazebo or ROS graph was run, and no hardware run is claimed. A RosDriver hardware backend would additionally refuse without a human hardware review.

LIMITS: the command input is the exact flat 60-array frame. It mixes rad, rad/s, N.m and two PD gains, and the pinned controller states no kp or kd bound, so the single input carries Limit.operator_required; without an overlay every command is refused with MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The URDF joint travel (-3.00..3.00 hip_x, -3.89..1.50 hip_y, -2.70..2.70 knee; dog_model/urdf/leg.xacro:58-60,106-108,155-157), 17 N.m effort and 40 rad/s velocity (dog_model/urdf/defines.xacro:29-30) are source facts, not a substitute for the per-element operator envelope. site-limits.example.json is an illustrative fake-only overlay (-0.1..0.1) that lets the in-process conformance run exercise the publication; it is not a device bound and must be replaced at deployment.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: a ROS-free mhs.bridge.ros_transport.RecordingRosTransport. It is an analytic contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic, and runs no ROS, rosbridge, Gazebo, ODE solver, controller, contacts or wall-clock loop. Fidelity is F0: engine 'analytic:ROS contract fake (no Gazebo physics)', determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0, reset none, no snapshot/restore. Joint positions, torso pose and IMU values are fixed placeholders. The first desired-position field of a publication is echoed into the placeholder base x so a test can see arrival; this is not physics and does not claim motion. Malformed JointState (missing position) is answered through the real native subscription path and produces MHS.RESOURCE.STATE_INVALID. The fake does not model the optional tail configuration. NOT COVERED: Gazebo physics, contacts, motor dynamics, the missing controller process, the fourteen-joint tail, TF, RViz, live ROS/rosbridge and hardware.

TESTS AND CLEANLINESS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six repository cases (reads, operator-required refusal, overlay publication, flat-frame arrival at the transport, malformed JointState, and the failed e-stop receipt); all six pass. The retained check_driver case reports the same G6/G8 stop gap, which is expected for this blocked package. The pinned clone at 1399108d258e964ef04850ddbfb6865dbd117000 was not modified (git status --porcelain is empty); no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.
